title: Tenant Zone Claims, Write Quarantine, and Cross-Region Replay Controls for Analytics Ingest
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Console backend currently streams ingest events (usage, token counts, traces) into a centralized analytics pipeline and replicates to regional mirrors. Customers with strict residency requirements need deterministic enforcement when tenant region metadata is ambiguous or when upstream placement changes. Current replication behavior can lead to writes landing in a non-authoritative region during transient state changes (e.g., tenant migration, zone claim propagation delays, or failover).

Goal: Add a tenant-zone claiming service and a write-quarantine + replay control surface so that the analytics ingestion path can: 1) reliably determine authoritative region for a tenant at write time, 2) quarantine ambiguous writes until claim resolution, and 3) support controlled replay to remote mirrors once claims are finalized. This must integrate with Console backend APIs and the replication orchestration layer, preserve ordering for each tenant stream, and surface status to operators and Console UX.

Proposed design (high level):
- Tenant Zone Claim Service: small, highly-available service that serves the authoritative mapping of tenant -> zone(s). Exposes a read-through cache with TTL and a write API used by the tenant placement pipeline. Stores claims in a strongly-consistent store (etcd-backed) to avoid split-brain.
- Ingest Quarantine Layer: at the edge of the analytics ingestion consumer, implement a quarantine queue for events where the tenant's zone claim is unknown, inconsistent, or in-transition. Quarantined events are persisted to a short-term durable event buffer (S3-backed partitioned store) tagged with a claim_version and arrival metadata.
- Cross-Region Replay Controls: a controller that drains quarantine buffers when the claim resolves, then replays events to the appropriate regional replication stream with idempotency keys and per-tenant sequence numbers to preserve ordering. Replay has rate limiting and backoff to avoid overload during mass migrations. Replay activity is logged to an audit stream.
- Console integration: add backend endpoints for (a) tenant claim status, (b) quarantine backlog metrics, (c) replay progress, and (d) an operator-run replay trigger with dry-run mode. Expose these in Console Console Analytics -> Residency panel.
- Failure modes & fallbacks: if claim service is unreachable, default policy is 'quarantine' for tenants with residency requirements; fallback to best-effort direct ingest only for tenants with no residency constraint (flag on tenant profile).

Acceptance criteria:
- Deterministic routing: No writes for tenants with a residency policy should be accepted into a non-authoritative region (validated by integration tests and canary).
- Quarantine correctness: Quarantined events are durably stored and can be replayed exactly-once to the target region (end-to-end test with synthetic load).
- Observability: Console shows per-tenant quarantine count, average quarantine latency, last claim_version, and replay progress.
- Performance: Common-case (tenant with known claim) adds <2ms median tail to ingest path.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy Tenant Zone Claim Service to staging and run canonicalization job to pre-populate claims for test tenants.
2) Enable read-only quarantine instrumentation in ingestion (no path changes) and collect metrics for 72h.
3) Enable quarantine-write mode for a small set of internal tenants; validate durability & replay.
4) Gradually enable for customer tenants with residency policies behind feature flag; run live replays for migration days.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests for claim resolution and cache invalidation semantics.
- Integration test harness simulating claim transitions and ensuring correct quarantine+replay.
- Load test: 100k events/s with 5% migrating tenants to measure replay/backpressure behavior.

Rollforward / rollback criteria:
- Rollforward if quarantine backlog < 5k events per region and median replay latency < 30s during canary.
- Rollback if replay error rate > 1% for two consecutive 5m windows or if any data is observed in a region outside of authoritative claims.

Operational runbooks:
- How to inspect quarantine backlog: link-> https://internal.redwood/console/analytics/quarantine (dashboard)
- How to trigger manual replay for a tenant: CLI: rwdctl analytics replay --tenant <id> --dry-run
- How to demote a claim in emergency: follow org-approved emergency claim protocol (see runbook link).

Open design questions / risks:
- Claim store scale: need to ensure low read latency under heavy ingest; may require regional caches per ingestion cluster.
- Ordering guarantees: per-tenant sequence numbers must be assigned consistently even when events are quarantined and replayed. Consider embedding an ingest-time sequence and a replay sequence to reconcile.
- Storage costs: short-term durable buffer retention window (default 48h) impacts S3 costs; team to propose retention policy and lifecycle rules.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Diego: spike on per-tenant sequence numbering and ordering reconciliation (ETA 2025-02-14).
- Asha: run cost estimate for 48h S3 buffer and lifecycle (ETA 2025-02-12).
- Platform: schedule architecture review for claim store consistency model 2025-02-16.

comments: 2025-02-10 | Asha Patel: Created ticket after post-mortem of tenant migration incident where ~1.2% of events were replicated to prior region during a late propagation window.

2025-02-11 | Diego Ramos: Completed spike on candidate storage options; leaning toward etcd primary for claims + region-level read caches. Observed <1ms median read with a 5s TTL on a 3-node cluster in staging.

2025-02-12 | PM (Leah Chen): Confirmed scope aligns with product request 'residency-deep' and prioritized for Q1 customer migrations. Asked to include Console UX hooks for manual replay and visibility.
2025-02-13 | Design review: Agreed to use S3 partitioned buffer with per-tenant prefix and a limited 48h retention. Action: provide lifecycle cost estimate. (Asha assigned)

2025-02-14 | Diego Ramos: Spike results uploaded (PR#4210). Identified ordering challenge when quarantining mid-stream; proposed adding ingest_sequence + replay_sequence as metadata. Need to validate reconciliation logic.
2025-02-15 | SRE (Nikita Verma): Raised concern about burst replays during failover; recommend adding token-bucket rate limiter in the replay controller and alerting on replay error saturation.

2025-02-17 | Asha Patel: Cost estimate posted (Confluence appendix). Estimated S3 cost for 48h buffer at current ingest rates ~$1,800/month across regions. Added lifecycle rule to transition older objects to IA after 6h.

2025-02-18 | Diego Ramos: Implemented initial claim service prototype and pushed dev branch. Integration tests for deterministic routing pass locally. Next: enable quarantine-read instrumentation in staging (step 2).
